title: Geopolitical and Emerging Risks for Boards
summary: An eight-module programme helping boards identify, debate and prepare for geopolitical and emerging risks, ending with a facilitated board scenario exercise.
intro: This training programme equips boards and directors to identify, debate and prepare for geopolitical and emerging risks: building horizon scanning into the board agenda, testing resilience through scenarios and setting risk appetite for an uncertain world.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give directors a structured way to think about risks that are hard to quantify and fast-moving, from geopolitical fragmentation and state-sponsored cyber attack to climate, AI and quantum computing. Participants leave able to challenge management's horizon scanning, use scenarios and stress tests to probe resilience, and shape the board's risk appetite and agenda accordingly.
sections.What It Covers: Horizon scanning and emerging-risk frameworks, geopolitics and economic fragmentation, sanctions and trade restrictions, cyber and state actors, critical third parties and concentration risk, climate and nature, AI and quantum computing, scenario planning and stress testing, and the board's risk appetite and agenda.
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors, especially members of risk and strategy committees
Executive directors, chief risk officers and senior managers responsible for strategy and emerging risk
Company secretaries, heads of governance and strategy teams supporting the board
Learning Objectives: Explain how emerging risks are identified, assessed and escalated to the board
Assess the firm's exposure to geopolitical fragmentation, sanctions and trade restrictions
Evaluate cyber, third-party and concentration risks linked to state actors and critical providers
Challenge management's response to climate, nature, AI and quantum risks
Use scenario planning and stress testing to test strategy and resilience
Set the board's risk appetite and agenda for emerging risks, and agree an action plan
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about two hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two-day programme or as a series of board briefing sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with scenarios and a board question set, the final module is a facilitated scenario exercise, and modules can be selected or tailored to the board's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No specialist knowledge of geopolitics, technology or climate science is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
G7 Cyber Expert Group, Public Statement on Planning for the Opportunities and Risks of Quantum Computing (2024)
TNFD, Recommendations of the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (2023)

modules.title: Horizon Scanning and Emerging-Risk Frameworks
modules.summary: How firms identify and assess risks that are uncertain, interconnected and slow to show in data, and what a good emerging-risk process looks like from the boardroom.
objectives: Explain the difference between emerging, principal and known risks
Evaluate the firm's horizon scanning and emerging-risk process
Identify blind spots, groupthink and signals the board may be missing
syllabus: Emerging risk taxonomies, risk radars and velocity
Sources of insight: internal data, external experts and supervisory publications
Interconnected risks and second-order effects
Questions to test whether horizon scanning reaches decisions

modules.title: Geopolitics, Fragmentation, Sanctions and Trade Restrictions
modules.summary: How geopolitical tension, economic fragmentation, sanctions and trade restrictions affect financial firms' markets, clients, operations and strategy, and how boards should respond.
objectives: Assess the firm's exposure to geopolitical events and fragmentation
Explain how sanctions and trade restrictions can disrupt business at short notice
Challenge management's country, client and supply-chain exposure analysis
syllabus: Geopolitical fragmentation, conflict and shifting alliances
Rapidly expanding sanctions, counter-sanctions and export controls
Market, credit, operational and conduct transmission channels
Exiting markets and clients: strategy, cost and customer impact

modules.title: Cyber, State Actors and Critical Third Parties
modules.summary: Why state-sponsored cyber activity and dependence on a small number of critical providers create severe but plausible scenarios, and what boards should require on resilience.
objectives: Recognise the threat from state actors and organised cyber groups
Assess concentration and dependency on critical third parties
Evaluate the firm's ability to withstand and recover from severe disruption
syllabus: State-sponsored attacks, disruption and supply-chain compromise
Cloud, data and infrastructure concentration risk
Severe but plausible scenarios and impact tolerances
Board questions on testing, exit plans and recovery

modules.title: Climate and Nature as Emerging Risks
modules.summary: How physical, transition and nature-related risks reach the firm's balance sheet, clients and operations, and how boards challenge the time horizons and assumptions used.
objectives: Explain physical, transition and nature-related risk channels
Challenge the time horizons and assumptions in climate risk analysis
Integrate climate and nature risk into strategy and risk appetite
syllabus: Physical, transition and liability risks
Nature loss and biodiversity as a financial risk
Climate scenarios and long-horizon uncertainty
Disclosure, transition planning and greenwashing risk

modules.title: AI, Quantum and Technological Disruption
modules.summary: The strategic and risk implications of AI, quantum computing and other disruptive technologies, including their use by competitors and criminals, and the decisions boards need to take now.
objectives: Assess strategic opportunity and disruption from AI and new entrants
Explain the quantum threat to cryptography and the migration timeline
Prioritise technology risks that need board decisions now
syllabus: AI-enabled competitors, fraud and misinformation
Quantum computing, harvest-now-decrypt-later and post-quantum migration
Business model disruption and technological lock-in
Board questions on readiness, investment and capability

modules.title: Scenario Planning and Stress Testing
modules.summary: How scenario planning and stress testing turn uncertain risks into decisions, how to judge whether scenarios are severe and imaginative enough, and how results should shape strategy.
objectives: Explain the difference between forecasting, scenario planning and stress testing
Challenge scenario severity, combination and management actions
Use results to inform strategy, capital and resilience decisions
syllabus: Narrative scenarios versus quantitative stress tests
Compound and cascading scenarios across risk types
Reverse stress testing and the limits of models
Turning scenario results into decisions and triggers

modules.title: Risk Appetite and the Board Agenda for Emerging Risks
modules.summary: How boards set risk appetite for risks that are hard to measure, decide what reaches the board agenda, and obtain the information and assurance they need.
objectives: Set qualitative and quantitative risk appetite for emerging risks
Design a board agenda and information flow that keeps emerging risks visible
Obtain challenge and assurance from the risk function, internal audit and external experts
syllabus: Risk appetite statements for hard-to-quantify risks
Board and committee agendas, deep dives and strategy days
Management information, early warning indicators and escalation
The board's own capability, diversity of thought and external advice

modules.title: Capstone: Board Scenario Exercise
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a facilitated board simulation in which participants respond to an evolving, multi-risk scenario and agree the board's emerging-risk priorities.
objectives: Apply the programme's tools to a live, evolving scenario
Make and communicate board decisions under uncertainty and time pressure
Produce a board action plan for emerging-risk oversight
syllabus: Scenario injects: geopolitical shock, cyber attack and third-party failure
Decision-making, escalation and stakeholder communication under pressure
Debrief: what the board knew, missed and should have asked
Workshop: the board's twelve-month emerging-risk plan

related.title: Board Effectiveness: Dynamics and Decision-Making
related.summary: A ten-module programme helping boards strengthen their dynamics, information and decision-making, and evidence effective oversight to supervisors.

related.title: Culture, Conduct and Accountability for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving boards the tools to shape and oversee culture, align incentives, hold individuals to account and evidence oversight to regulators.

related.title: Effective Governance for Boards and Directors
related.summary: A twelve-module programme covering the standards expected of individual directors and the practices that make a board effective, for regulated firms, fund boards and management companies.

related.title: Finance and Prudential Essentials for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving non-financial directors the confidence to read a regulated firm's accounts, capital and liquidity position, and to challenge the CFO.

related.title: Group Governance and Cross-Border Operations
related.summary: A nine-module programme helping boards and senior managers of cross-border groups balance group direction with local accountability, oversee intragroup arrangements and deal with multiple supervisors.

related.title: Induction for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: A ten-module induction giving new directors of regulated firms the grounding to discharge their duties, understand supervisory expectations and oversee the firm's risks.
